parsed.summary: Two existence statements are formalized. (1) There are two finitely generated, countable, ICC groups with Kazhdan property (T) whose group von Neumann algebras are trace-preservingly *-isomorphic but which are not isomorphic as groups. (2) There are a group Λ and a sequence (Γ_n) of finitely generated property-(T) groups, all with group factor isomorphic to L(Λ), that are pairwise non-isomorphic and none isomorphic to Λ. The most important caveat is that (2) asserts ICC for Λ but only for *some* Γ_n (`∃ n, IsICC (Γ n)`), not for all; the paper's index-24^n commensurability claim is also not formalized.

glossary.plain: The *-isomorphism and its inverse preserve suprema of arbitrary families of projections.
glossary.note: This is an ad hoc encoding of normality. It is automatic for any *-isomorphism, so it is only an extra (satisfiable) requirement.

glossary.plain: There is a *-algebra isomorphism L(G) ≅ L(H) that satisfies the normality condition above and preserves the canonical traces.
glossary.standard_concept: isomorphism of group von Neumann algebras L(G) ≅ L(H)
glossary.note: The extra conditions are automatic for II_1 factors, where *-isomorphisms are normal and the trace is unique. They only strengthen an existential claim.

lean_claims.plain: There exist countable groups Γ, Λ with the following properties: both are finitely generated, both are ICC, both have property (T), L(Γ) ≅ L(Λ) (normal, trace-preserving *-isomorphism), and Γ ≇ Λ.

There exist a countable group Λ and countable groups Γ_n (n ∈ ℕ) with the following properties: Λ and all Γ_n are finitely generated; Λ is ICC; some Γ_n is ICC; Λ and all Γ_n have property (T); L(Γ_n) ≅ L(Λ) and L(Γ_m) ≅ L(Γ_n) for all m, n; Γ_m ≇ Γ_n for m ≠ n; and Λ ≇ Γ_n for all n.

paper_claims.plain: There exist countable ICC property-(T) groups Λ, Γ_0 with L(Λ) ≅ L(Γ_0) and Λ ≇ Γ_0.

There exist f.g. ICC property-(T) groups Λ, Γ_0, Γ_1, … that are pairwise nonisomorphic with L(Γ_n) ≅ L(Λ) for all n. Moreover, Γ_n contains a subgroup isomorphic to Γ_0 of index 2^{4n}, so the Γ_n are commensurable.

coverage.why: It adds finite generation and normality/trace-preservation of the isomorphism; all of these hold for the paper's examples.
ICC is asserted for Λ but only for some Γ_n, not for every Γ_n.
No subgroup or index statement appears.

flags.explanation: `(∃ n, IsICC (Γ n))` requires only one Γ_n to be ICC, whereas the paper asserts that every Γ_n is ICC. Mathematically, ICC of Γ_n follows from L(Γ_n) ≅ L(Λ) being a factor. However, the formal statement as written is weaker than the paper and does not directly assert the infinite ICC fiber.

flags.explanation: The isomorphism of group factors is encoded as an algebraic *-isomorphism with an ad hoc projection-supremum normality condition and trace preservation. Both extra conditions are automatic for II_1 factors, so this only strengthens the existential claim relative to plain L(G) ≅ L(H).

Property (T) quantifies only over Hilbert spaces in the same universe as G (Type 0). For countable groups this is equivalent to the standard definition, since one can reduce to separable subrepresentations.
